sections.overview: This small swiftlet is native to Java, Bali, Lombok and nearby islands, with populations also in Sumatra.
sections.identification: It has dark, green-glossed upperparts, a pale belly and square-cut tail, and is easily confused with other swiftlets.
sections.habitat: It forages over varied lowland and upland habitats and nests in caves.
sections.diet: It catches small flying insects in the air while in continuous, fast flight.
sections.behavior: It is active in groups. Indonesian observers describe rapid, erratic flight and chattering calls near nesting sites.
sections.reproduction: Swiftlets build small bracket nests on sheltered vertical surfaces, using saliva with plant material.
sections.ecology: It is distinct from the Glossy Swiftlet, Collocalia esculenta; the Kinabalu swiftlet is now treated separately as Collocalia dodgei.
sections.conservation: BirdLife lists the species as Least Concern; local abundance and trends are not uniform across the islands.
